# Marker

A divider or status line inside a conversation, such as a date or someone joining.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill odv-pill-out">Left out of Multi-brand</span> Multi-brand draws on core, content and media families, not conversation. It admits only families in its roles. Its only messages go to support through a textarea. <span class="odv-instead">Use instead: <a href="./separator">Separator</a></span></p>

## When to use it

- **Use it when:** Breaking a long conversation into days or showing events in it.
- **Not when:** A message someone wrote.

Instead:

- [Message](./message.md): Something someone said.

## Words

- Shared structure: object, state, next step.
- Brand tone lives in headlines and marketing copy, not in errors.
- Errors and confirmations read the same in every brand.
- Use: Get started, Plan, Order. Avoid: Brand-specific words in errors, Jargon.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Cancel
- `content.action.destroy`: Remove
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Get started

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add marker
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Tokens it reads

Marker reads 1 of Multi-brand's tokens. Each row follows one part of the component from its class to the value it ends at, in every theme. Change a token in the scheme and every component that reads it follows.
